attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' tied to the condition that scammers spread photorealistic fake videos. The normalised wording keeps that condition. The nearby 'will likely' sentence is a separate claim and is correctly left out.

contract.note: 'No idea' is hyperbole. Reading it as near-chance accuracy, or most viewers unable to tell reliably, is an ordinary plain reading. A 75% bar for contradiction is fair. Results in the 60-66% band leave it unclear which way the claim falls.

evidence.note: Runway study, 1,043 participants, 57.1% accuracy, over 90% not reliable. Dated before the cutoff and has stated methods. But the vendor is grading its own model's realism, so it is a company disclosure and is given less weight.

Academic preprint. Fakes from modern generators were spotted 52.6% of the time, near chance. Real clips scored about 73%, so overall accuracy is about 63%. The sample was mostly technical students. Partial independent support.

Peer-reviewed study, 1,276 participants, near-chance accuracy across media types. Data comes from early 2024, before AI video was common on platforms, so it gives only weak support for the conditional forecast.
Small lab study (n=40) with primed viewers: mean 66.4%, most above 50%. This is counterevidence but stays well below the contract's 75% bar for contradiction.
Kapwing measurement: 21% of the Shorts served to a new YouTube account were AI-generated. This shows the condition was met. It does not show the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The condition is met (e5). No study reaches the 75% bar for contradiction. The large Runway study (Jan 2026) meets the early-resolution rule at 57% accuracy, with over 90% of viewers not reliable. It comes from a vendor, but the independent preprint e2 (fakes at chance) and e3 point the same way. e4 at 66% has a small sample of primed viewers. On the fair plain reading, the evidence supports the claim, with the caveat that the main study came from a vendor.
